remit: X12 defines this reason as precertification, authorization, notification or pre-treatment approval being absent.
metaDescription: CO-197 denial explained: precertification, authorization or notification was absent. How to request a retro authorization, appeal, and prevent it up front.
summary: The payer denied the claim because a required prior authorization or notification was not obtained.
causes: Authorization was not requested before the service
The authorization was requested but the number did not reach the claim
The authorization had expired or did not cover the service billed
fixes: Check whether an authorization exists and matches the service and dates
If it exists, correct the claim with the number and resubmit
If not, ask the payer whether a retroactive authorization or an appeal is allowed
prevention: Keep a list of services that need authorization by payer
Block scheduling for those services until the authorization is on file

faqs.question: Can a CO-197 denial be reversed after the service?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. Some payers allow retroactive authorization in limited cases. Many do not, so prevention matters most.

faqs.question: Who should track authorizations?
faqs.answer: A named person on the front-end team. Zenith's care coordinators can handle authorization requests and follow-up inside your EHR.
